    Spain

    Spain offers affordable public university education (even for non-EU), a sunny Mediterranean climate, and a vibrant student culture. Strong in business (IE, IESE, ESADE), tourism, renewable energy (Iberdrola), and Spanish-language studies. The 2022 immigration reform expanded post-study work rights.

    Overview

    Spain offers affordable public university education (even for non-EU), a sunny Mediterranean climate, and a vibrant student culture. Strong in business (IE, IESE, ESADE), tourism, renewable energy (Iberdrola), and Spanish-language studies. The 2022 immigration reform expanded post-study work rights.

    Education system

    Public universities (universidades públicas), private universities, and distance learning (UNED). Bologna: Grado (4yr, 240 ECTS), Máster Universitario (1–2yr, 60–120 ECTS), Doctorado (3yr). Distinctive: Título propio (institutional Master's, not state-recognised) vs Título oficial.

    Study levels

    bachelorsmastersphdpostdocdiploma

    businessmbatourismrenewable-energyarchitecturespanish-languageengineeringhospitalityart

    Tuition fee range

    Public (comunidad autónoma): €750–€2,500/year EU, €1,000–€4,000/year non-EU (varies by region — Catalonia/Madrid highest); private €5,000–€25,000/year; top business schools €30,000–€70,000/year

    Per academic year, varies by institution.

    Living cost range

    €700–€1,100/month; Madrid/Barcelona €900–€1,400/month; smaller cities €600–€900/month

    Per year, includes accommodation + food.

    Major student cities

    MadridBarcelonaValenciaSevilleGranadaSalamancaBilbaoMalaga

    Admission requirements

    UG: high school diploma equivalent to Spanish Título de Bachiller + university entrance exam (EBAU/EvAU, or UNEDasised for non-EU); some programmes require specific access tests. PG: relevant Grado degree (180–240 ECTS). PhD: Master's + research plan + supervisor.

    English requirements

    English programmes: IELTS 6.0–7.0, TOEFL iBT 80–100. Spanish programmes: DELE B2 (UG), C1 (PG).

    Available intakes

    Autumn (September, primary), Spring (February, limited).

    Application deadlines

    • Public UG via distrito único: June–July. PG: Feb–Jun (varies by university). PhD: rolling.

    Student visa overview

    Non-EU: Type D student visa (Visado de Estudios) at Spanish consulate. For >180 days, also need Autorización de Estancia por Estudios (residence permit) processed on arrival at Oficina de Extranjería. EU: register at central de extranjería for NIE.

    Financial evidence

    Proof of €7,992/year (IPREM 2024 × 12, 100%) via bank statement, sponsor, or scholarship. Paid work authorization required separately if working part-time.

    Work rights

    Non-EU students: 30 hours/week part-time (with prior authorisation from Extranjería). EU: full work rights. Minimum wage SMI €1,134/month (2024, 14 pays).

    Post-study opportunities

    12-month residence permit for job-seeking (Autorización de residencia para búsqueda de empleo) for Bachelor's+/Master's graduates of Spanish institutions (2022 reform). 24-month permit for PhD graduates. Pathway to work permit.

    Accommodation

    Colegio Mayor (€400–€800/month, limited, often for first-year), shared flat (piso compartido) €250–€450/month, studio €500–€900/month. Madrid/Barcelona 30–50% higher.

    Healthcare

    Non-EU: private health insurance mandatory for visa (€300–€500/year). EU: EHIC valid, can register with Spanish SSN. Public healthcare free at point of use once registered.

    Transport

    Metro de Madrid, TMB (Barcelona), EMT buses — monthly abono joven (~€20–€55/month under-26). Renfe Cercanías, AVE high-speed rail. BiciMAD/bicing bike share.

    Student safety

    Generally safe; petty theft in tourist hubs (Las Ramblas, Sol). Emergency: 112, 091 (national police), 061 (ambulance).

    Cultural info

    Spanish (Castilian), Catalan, Basque, Galician co-official in regions. Tapas culture, siesta (less common now), flamenco, fútbol (Real Madrid/Barça), late dining (lunch 14:00, dinner 21:30), fiesta tradition. Climate 8–35°C.

    Application process

    1) Non-EU: pre-enroll via UNEDasised (credentials recognition + entrance exam). 2) Apply to university via distrito único portal. 3) Receive admission. 4) Apply Type D visa at consulate. 5) Arrive, apply for residence permit (TIE) at Oficina de Extranjería. 6) Register empadronamiento (census).

    Required documents

    • Passport
    • legalised/apostilled + sworn-translated transcripts
    • degree certificates
    • English/Spanish test scores
    • statement of purpose
    • CV
    • passport photos
    • proof of funds
    • private health insurance
    • criminal record check.
